title: do and make
subtitle: do the shopping / make a mistake
summary: Use do for actions in general and make when somebody produces or creates something, and learn the common phrases with each verb.

lesson.heading: do = a general word for actions
lesson.text: **Do** is a general word for actions. When we do not say the name of the action, we use **do**.

examples.text: *A:* Shall I open the window? *B:* No, it's OK. I'll **do** it.
Rachel's job is very boring. She **does** the same thing every day.
I **did** a lot of things yesterday.

lesson.heading: What do you do?
lesson.text: **What do you do?** is a question about your job. It means: What's your job?

examples.text: *A:* What do you **do**? *B:* I work in a bank.

lesson.heading: make = produce or create
lesson.text: **Make** = produce or create. Something new is there at the end. A woman with a coffee pot in her hands is **making** coffee. A man with a big cake in his hands has **made** a cake.

left.label: do (an action)
left.text: You do an action. Nothing new is there at the end.
examples: I **did** a lot yesterday. I cleaned my room and I wrote some letters.
*A:* What do you **do** in your free time? Sport? Reading?
I **did** the washing, but I didn't **do** the shopping.

right.label: make (something new)
right.text: You make something, so something new is there at the end.
examples: *B:* I **make** clothes. I **make** dresses and jackets.
I also **make** toys for my children.

lesson.heading: Expressions with do
rows: I'm **doing my driving test** next week.
John has just **done a training course**.
Our children have to **do** a lot of **homework**.
Sue, could you **do me a favour**?
I go for a run and **do exercises** every morning.
lesson.note: Also *do the shopping / do the washing / do the washing-up / do the ironing / do the cooking*: I **did the washing**, but I didn't **do the shopping**.

lesson.heading: Expressions with make
rows: I need to **make an appointment** to see the doctor.
Excuse me, I have to **make a phone call**.
Sometimes I forget to **make my bed** in the morning.

lesson.text: We say **make a film** but **take a photograph**: *When was this film made?* but *When was this photograph taken?*

exercises.prompt: What did you ___ at the weekend? Did you go away?
exercises.explanation: We do not name the action, so we use do.

exercises.prompt: Do you know how to ___ bread?
exercises.explanation: You produce bread, so we use make.
Somebody produces paper, so we use make: paper is made from wood.

exercises.prompt: *A:* What do you ___? *B:* I'm a doctor.
exercises.explanation: What do you do? is a question about your job.

exercises.prompt: I asked you to clean the bathroom. Have you ___ it?
exercises.explanation: After have we use done, the past participle of do.

exercises.prompt: Which verb goes with each expression: do or make?
What are these people doing? Match each situation with the right sentence.

pairs.left: A man is putting flour, eggs and milk in a bowl.
Two children are writing in an exercise book after school.
A man is putting food in a basket at the supermarket.
A woman is standing at the sink with plates and water.
A man is writing sugar, bread, tea and milk on a piece of paper.
A man is holding a camera in front of his face.

exercises.prompt: Why do you always ___ the same mistake?
I need to see the dentist, but I haven't ___ an appointment.
exercises.explanation: We say make an appointment, so after haven't we use made.

exercises.statement: It was a bad mistake. It was the worst mistake I've ever done.
exercises.explanation: It was the worst mistake I've ever made. We say make a mistake, not do a mistake.

exercises.prompt: There's something wrong with the car. The engine is ___ a strange noise.
Put the words in the right order.
exercises.answer: Let's make a list of all the things we have to do today.
exercises.explanation: make a list (you produce the list), but do things (a general action).
